q: In Windows NT, what does NT stand for?
explain: NT stands for New Technology; modern desktop Windows belongs to the NT family.

q: Which statement about Windows 11 is correct?
options: It is offered in both 32-bit and 64-bit editions
It is a graphical shell that runs over MS-DOS
It works only on touch-screen devices
It is 64-bit only but can run many compatible 32-bit applications
explain: Windows 10 had 32-bit and 64-bit editions, but Windows 11 is 64-bit only while still running many compatible 32-bit apps.

q: Which system, used on the IBM 704 in 1956, is commonly cited as the first operating system?
explain: GM-NAA I/O was developed by General Motors Research and North American Aviation to improve batch processing.

q: On which date was Windows 1.0 released?
explain: Windows 1.0 appeared on 20 November 1985 as a graphical environment over MS-DOS. The other dates belong to Windows 95, Vista and Windows 11.

q: Windows Explorer and My Computer first arrived with which Windows version?
explain: Windows 95 (public launch 24 August 1995) introduced Windows Explorer and My Computer.

q: Windows Vista had its worldwide consumer launch on which date?
explain: Vista reached businesses in 2006 and launched worldwide for consumers on 30 January 2007.

q: Windows 8 removed the traditional desktop Start button. Which version brought that button back?
explain: Windows 8.1 restored the Start button, while Windows 10 later restored a redesigned Start menu.

q: What was the general release date of Windows 11?
explain: 24 June 2021 was the unveiling and 31 August 2021 was when the availability date was announced; general release was 5 October 2021.

q: Standard support for Windows 10 ended on which date?
explain: Standard Windows 10 support ended on 14 October 2025; extended-security and specialised editions have separate terms.

q: Which of the following is NOT a standard system-status indicator in the system tray?
explain: The system tray (notification area) shows items such as network, volume, battery, security and printing status; Microsoft Office Suite is not one.

q: What happens when you click the Minimize button of a window?
options: The app closes and unsaved work is lost
The window is hidden but the app stays open
The window fills the available work area
The window returns to its earlier size
explain: Minimize hides the window while the app keeps running; its taskbar button restores it. Maximize fills the work area and Restore Down returns the earlier size.

q: Which statement about the taskbar in standard Windows 11 is correct?
options: It stays at the bottom, and its icons can align left or centre
It can be docked on any screen edge in standard settings
It always sits on the left edge with centred icons
It is another name for the Action Center
explain: Windows 10 and many earlier versions let the taskbar sit on any edge, but standard Windows 11 keeps it at the bottom.

q: Which command typed into the Run box opens File Explorer?
explain: Type explorer or explorer.exe in Run. Windows + E is a keyboard shortcut, not text to type into Run.

q: Which File Explorer folder view shows columns such as Name, Type, Size and Date modified?
explain: The Details view lists items in columns. List is a compact list, Tiles adds extra information beside icons, and Content shows descriptive information.

q: What does Shift + Delete do to a selected file?
options: Sends it to the Recycle Bin
Securely erases it so recovery is impossible
Bypasses the Recycle Bin without guaranteeing secure erasure
explain: Shift + Delete skips the Recycle Bin, but it does not guarantee secure erasure or prevent recovery.

q: Which of these characters cannot normally be used inside a Windows filename?
explain: Nine characters are not allowed: \ / : * ? " < > and |. Spaces, hyphens and underscores are fine.

q: NTFS was introduced in 1993 with which Windows version?
explain: NTFS (New Technology File System) came with Windows NT 3.1 in 1993.

q: Which statement about NTFS is correct?
options: A file can use ordinary NTFS compression and EFS encryption at the same time
NTFS is a document format used for Word files
Journaling records file-system changes to assist recovery
NTFS is supported only by Windows 11
explain: Journaling helps recovery. A file system is not a document format, compression and EFS cannot be combined on one file, and NT-based releases from 2000 onward support NTFS.

q: How many connecting devices could Windows XP Home allow for resource sharing?
explain: XP Home allowed 5 connecting devices and XP Professional allowed 10.

q: For Windows 7, 8, 10 and 11, the common exam figure of 20 in resource sharing refers to what?
options: Files open at the same time
explain: The figure concerns incoming sharing connections; it does not mean 20 desktop users or 20 open files.

q: Which of the following is NOT a standard Windows startup mode?
explain: Turbo Mode does not exist as a standard Windows startup mode. The other three are real Safe Mode options.

q: In Windows 10 or 11, how do you open the recovery options that lead to Startup Settings?
options: Press F8 repeatedly before Windows loads
Press Win + R at the desktop
Press Alt + F4 on the desktop
explain: Hold Shift while clicking Restart, then use Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Settings. F8 is the older Windows 7 style and is not universal.

q: On a BIOS-based system, in which order do the Windows boot files run?
explain: BIOS systems use bootmgr, then winload.exe, then ntoskrnl.exe. The .efi files belong to the UEFI sequence.

q: Which built-in Windows feature filters network traffic according to security rules?
explain: Windows Firewall filters network traffic and helps block unauthorised connections; Microsoft Defender Antivirus handles malware.

q: Which pair correctly describes Windows encryption tools?
options: BitLocker encrypts single files; EFS encrypts whole drives
Both BitLocker and EFS create spare backup copies
BitLocker encrypts supported drives; EFS encrypts individual files on NTFS
EFS works only on FAT32 volumes; BitLocker only on USB sticks
explain: BitLocker protects drives or volumes while EFS protects individual files on NTFS. Neither is a backup; encryption protects confidentiality.

q: System Restore is mainly used to do which of the following?
options: Roll back system files, drivers and Registry settings
Recover files emptied from the Recycle Bin
explain: Restore points roll back system changes. System Restore is not a personal-file backup and differs from restoring a document from the Recycle Bin.

q: Which statement about Bitdefender is correct?
options: Every Bitdefender product is completely free
Bitdefender is the antivirus built into Windows
Safepay is a disk defragmentation tool
Bitdefender Antivirus Free for Windows is a free tier, while other editions are paid
explain: Only the Antivirus Free tier is free. Safepay is its secure-browsing feature, and the built-in antivirus is Microsoft Defender.

q: Which statement correctly compares Sleep and Hibernate?
options: Sleep keeps the session mainly in RAM and resumes quickly; Hibernate saves it to storage and resumes more slowly
Sleep saves the session to storage; Hibernate keeps it in RAM
Hibernate resumes faster than Sleep but uses more power
Both options switch the PC off completely and discard the session
explain: Sleep suits short breaks and resumes fast; Hibernate writes the session to storage, uses less power and suits longer breaks.

q: Which file does Windows usually use as its paging file for virtual memory?
explain: pagefile.sys stores some memory pages outside physical RAM, but it is not as fast as RAM.

q: Which command opens the Windows Registry Editor?
explain: regedit opens the Registry Editor; services.msc opens the Services console and cmd.exe opens Command Prompt.

q: Which Windows tool removes selected temporary and unnecessary files to free storage?
explain: Disk Cleanup deletes junk files. Optimize Drives (defragmentation) only optimises how data is stored.

q: Which folder holds essential Windows executables, libraries and drivers, typically at C:\Windows?
explain: System32 contains core Windows components. Program Files holds installed apps, Users holds profiles, and Temp holds temporary data.

q: In Windows 11, which shortcut opens Snap Layouts?
explain: Win + Z opens Snap Layouts (or hover over Maximize). Win + V is clipboard history and Win + A is Quick Settings.

q: Pressing which key five times invokes the Sticky Keys shortcut when it is enabled?
explain: Pressing Shift five times offers Sticky Keys, an accessibility feature that lets you press modifier-key combinations one key at a time.

q: In Windows 11, the Win + A shortcut opens which panel?
explain: In Windows 11 Win + A opens Quick Settings (Windows 10 opened Action Center); Win + N opens Notification Center and calendar.

q: WordPad was removed from Windows starting with which version?
explain: WordPad, a basic formatted-document editor, was removed starting with Windows 11 version 24H2, so it is now a historical answer.

q: Which shortcut performs a hard reload of a webpage in Chrome on Windows?
explain: Ctrl + F5 is a hard reload. F5 and Ctrl + R are normal reloads, and Win + R opens the Run dialog.

q: Which of the following is Microsoft's web search engine rather than a web browser?
explain: Bing is a search engine that finds information online; Edge and Internet Explorer are browsers that display web pages.
